text: The rwb-case case read and closure answer, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision package read are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them; the four rows are class C dependencies in fact although the plan's C row for this slice is None.
why: Only rwb-case writes recovery_case, timer, assignment and task, only rwb-access answers the capability area and the right, and only rwb-decision governs the UNIVERSAL and DEBTSALE rule rows and their ledger. TSD S6 T5.2 names the cross-module calls only as published interfaces and publishes no operation name for the case read, the closure answer or the authorise call, so no name may be invented. Keeping the plan's C row unchanged and recording the rows as tracked dependencies is the only choice that does not invent a metadata value.

text: The closure step publishes no REST operation of its own: it is signalled by the award operation API-S6-003 of RWB-S6-E6005-APP, and its closure element is declared as a read-only element embedded in the lot read answer API-S6-002 and in the composite answer of SCR-26 Award, with its property set and required flags settled in the baseline review.
why: TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for the module and none is a case closure, and the single endpoint row of the legacy story is the award path, which is the award story's in the target. No source publishes a closure element schema, so the element's field set is a design choice while the end state and the list values come from the rule book. Claiming an operation of a sibling would break the ownership rule of the Ownership Map.

text: R-UNI-47 is applied to every case whose account is in the awarded lot, from any non-terminal state, and the instruction to stop every open action is applied by the owners on their boundaries: rwb-case cancels its own tasks, timers and open actions, rwb-deviation closes its open deviation against the sold case, and the parent CaseWorkflow cancels the open stage children, while this service sends only the case reference, the end state CASE_CLOSED_SOLD and the rule with its version.
why: The from state of R-UNI-47 is ANY_ACTIVE, defined as any non-terminal state on any route, which covers a case whose only route is the debt sale as well as one that sits on another route, while the condition text names another route. Neither the FSD nor the rule book enumerates the open actions to be stopped, and no service may write or cancel another service's rows or timers under DP-01 and DP-12, so the set is applied inside each owner's boundary rather than by this service.

text: The unattended closure runs under the rwb-debtsale service identity, and the Debt sale right A of the legacy permission row stays with RW-DEBTSALE, RW-PRODHEAD and RW-HEADASL on the award operation and the read of the closure element; no right is declared for the closure step itself.
why: The FSD makes the feature unattended (A2.14.3.3, 'None; runs unattended'), while the legacy permission table gives the Debt sale right A to three human roles and TSD S6 T6.1 gives the service identities SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES and SY-AGENT the right R only. Reading the three sources together, the right belongs to the surfaces a person or a caller uses and not to the unattended step, and inventing a right for the step would break the RBAC matrix.

text: The ALS and GL integration points of FEAT-DBS-14 are the derecognition under R-DS-30 and the general ledger posting under R-DS-31 of FEAT-DBS-12, owned by RWB-S6-E6008-APP; the closure story posts nothing, holds no adapter and reads no balance, and the account data transfer named in R-UNI-47 is R-DS-29 in RWB-S6-E6007-APP.
why: The feature table of the Epics 3 to 8 Specification names 'Workbench, ALS and GL' for FEAT-DBS-14, but no rule of the closure writes to ALS or the ledger: R-UNI-47 stops the open actions and closes the case as sold, R-DS-29 transfers the data, and R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 derecognise and post. DP-16 is not in the pattern set of this key, so no rwb-integration contract row may be added to the metadata, and the two integration points are recorded against the sibling stories.
